newsitem.title: UK: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest - May 2.
newsitem.headline: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest - May 2.

text.p: REUTERS EMERGING EUROPE PRESS DIGEST FOR ADVERTISING & MEDIA
Weekly Press Digest from Central and Eastern Europe on Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Markets
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

-- Russian ad agencies have signed a charter to regulate principles of co-operation and competition. Sergei Samoshin, PR department head at Premier SV, one of Russia's biggest ad agencies, says the charter will have no legal force but will act as a kind of gentlemen's agreement. (Kommersant Daily, May 14, 1997)

-- The seven biggest public relations firms in Poland handled business worth $5 million in the first three quarters of 1996. "The market is developing at an intensive rate and the number of customers and contracts grows year on year", says Jerzy Ciszewski of Ciszewski PR. (Dziennik Prawa i Gospodarki, May 9, 1997)

-- Advertising agency Head II has been awarded the Teacher's whisky ad account in the Czech Republic. It will run a campaign this summer in magazines, on the radio, in bars and in shops. It will also be promoting a competition to win a trip to Scotland.
(Strategie News, May 7-14, 1997)
-- Pepsi is sponsoring six concerts by top Czech pop group, Lucie. (Strategie News, May 7-14, 1997)

-- The Czech Association of Advertising Agencies and the Czech federation for brand-name products are lobbying against a request from TV Nova to restrict considerably the number of TV commercials on public-television broadcasts. (Pravo, May 12, 1997)
-- Czech researchers IP Praha estimate some 3.7 billion crowns ($120.3 million) was spent on TV ads in the Czech Republic last year and investments in outdoor ads exceeded one billion crowns.
(Pravo, May 12, 1997)

-- The winner of the contest for the best Czech print advertisement was an ad for Skoda Octavia cars created by ad agency Grey Praha. The best public relations campaign was developed by Bates/Saatchi & Saatchi for the Winterthur insurance company, the Publisher's Union says. (Hospodarske Noviny, May 14, 1997)
-- Czech advertising agency Relax, is launching a campaign for radio station Radio Relax, to celebrate its second year on air. (Strategie News, May 7-14, 1997)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

-- Czech company Beseda Holding confirms it is interested in obtaining a majority stake in the second largest nation-wide private Czech television station, Prima TV. Beseda Holding is currently partially tied to the television station Nova, which made 1.2 billion crowns in pre-tax profits last year. (Strategie News, May 7-14, 1997)

-- The Bulgarian private television station Nova Televisia said it had cut its advertisement rates by 30 percent from April 1 to compete with state Bulgarian National Television. At present 30 seconds of prime time on Nova Televisia costs $385.
(Pari, May 15, 1997)

-- Bulgarias Commission for Protection of Competition said it may file a monopoly suit against Germanys Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitung (WAZ) press group which has bought the two biggest Bulgarian press groups -- 168 Hours and Media Holding.
Under Bulgarian law WAZ could be fined one million levs ($645) and the deal to buying Media Holding could be cancelled. (Pari, May 14, 1997)

-- Poland puts $3.0 million a year into subsidising its national film industry, which enables the industry to produce up to six medium-budget films, the Independent Film and TV Producers' Association said. (Gazeta Bankowa, May 11, 1997)

-- The Czech parliament is in a heated dispute over changes to the law on radio and television broadcasting. It is debating demands by Czech broadcaster Nova Television, that advertisements on public Ceska Televize be restricted.
(Hospodarske Noviny, May 15, 1997)

-- Nova Television controlled 71.5 percent of the Czech market for television advertising for the first quarter of this year. It was followed by Ceska Televize with 24.5 percent, Prima with three percent and Cable Plus with 0.12 percent, according to research company A-Connect. (Strategie News, May 7-14, 1997)
-- Contestants in the Miss Czech Republic contest were presented on the Internet for the first time allowing Internet users to vote for their favourites. (Strategie News, May 7-14, 1997)

-- Czech Internet company Seznam launches a full-text Czech navigation tool called Kompas which searches on the World Wide Web and it solves problems related to words with Czech accent marks.(Pravo, May 14, 1997)
-- Poland will host the 42 International Book Fair in Warsaw this month, with over 1,340 publishers expected to take part, fair organisers say. (Dziennik Prawa i Gospodarki, May 15, 1997
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

-- Unilever's Hungarian unit Magyarorszag Kt has agreed to buy three brands from Hungarian cosmetics and toiletries company Caola Rt and will invest one billion forints ($5.5 million) in Caola Rt. (Napi Gazdasag, May 14, 1997)

-- Hungarian fruit juice producer Sotex Kft, which bottles French brandy under the Napoleon Andre Renard brandname, plans to import and bottle original Scotch from Scotland. The company supplies multinational supermarket chains. (Napi Gazdasag, May 12, 1997)
-- South Korea's consumer electronics giant Samsung, plans to invest $200 million in plants in Poland and Hungary, a company spokesman said. (Gazeta Wyborcza, May 13, 1997)
-- Toiletries company Schwarzkopf & Henkel has launched a new line of hair dyes on the Czech market called Poly Country Colors, backed by a campaign created by ad agency Hager.
(Strategie News, May 7-14, 1997)
-- The Czech Pavilion shopping mall in Prague has won an award for the best marketing programme at the annual conference of the International Council of Shopping Centres in Lisbon.
(Hospodarske Noviny, May 14, 1997)
CONSUMER TRENDS:
-- Polish consumers deposit on average between 3,000 zlotys ($951) and 4,000 zlotys when they open an investment account, a report by the Atut investment trust said. (Gazeta Bankowa, May 11, 1997).
-- Poles are avid readers and the book market grows by 20 percent every year, the Polish publishing industry said. This year book sales may exceed 1.0 billion zlotys. (Zycie, May 15, 1997)
